title: SVM on serum metabolite profiles distinguishes oral squamous cell carcinoma
summary: Serum from 819 volunteers (578 OSCC patients, 241 healthy controls) was profiled by conductive polymer spray ionization mass spectrometry. Univariate analysis selected 65 candidate metabolite ions, and DESI-MS imaging confirmed that 8 of the top 10 showed the same trends in tissue and serum. A support vector machine separated OSCC from controls with 98.0% accuracy by cross-validation in the discovery cohort and 89.2% in the validation cohort. The design is case-control, the validation cohort size is not in the abstract, and univariate selection precedes the machine learning step.
ai_technology: Support vector machine classifier on serum metabolite profiles

evidence.tested: Separate validation cohort and in situ tissue confirmation of metabolite trends.
evidence.unknown: Validation cohort size and performance in screening populations; preprint not peer reviewed; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Automatic prediction of OSCC from metabolite profiles
